patch_description: Replace the exponentially-weighted moving average with a two-stage hybrid: (1) a 1D Kalman filter with adaptive process noise (larger Q when innovation magnitude suggests genuine dynamics change, smaller Q when noise-dominated) to smooth noise with near-zero lag, followed by (2) a Savitzky-Golay smoothing filter that fits local low-order polynomials, preserving signal trends and slopes without the phase delay of MA filters. The Kalman stage makes the output statistically optimal for Gaussian noise; the SG stage suppresses slope changes and false reversals. The adaptive Q gate based on normalized innovation squared (NIS) keeps responsiveness during genuine trend changes while damping noise-induced reversals. Both filters are O(1)/O(window) per sample and causal alignment is maintained by the windowing convention already used.
